title: Non-linear pricing and optimal shipping policies
summary_en: Online retailers commonly bundle product price with shipping fee, sometimes hiding shipping behind a flat 'free delivery' threshold. Tóbiás models nonlinear pricing where the seller chooses both the per-unit price and the shipping-fee schedule, and characterises when bundling shipping into the unit price dominates a separate fee. The paper rationalises observed pricing patterns (free-shipping thresholds, fixed delivery fees) and identifies the consumer-welfare consequences of each design.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; the analysis is a nonlinear-pricing model with consumer search and shipping-cost trade-offs.
policy_relevance: Useful framing for Hungarian and EU consumer-protection policy and digital-markets regulation (Magyar Posta tariff oversight, EU DSA / DMA): when online sellers strategically combine price and shipping-fee schedules, naive comparison-shopping tools can mislead consumers. The paper supports requirements that price-comparison platforms display total-cost (including shipping) figures by default.
